lines.text: New cars averaged over $50,000 in August 2026.
lines.say: New cars averaged over fifty thousand dollars in August twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: And the sticker price is only one of four numbers that decide what a buyer really pays.
lines.say: And the sticker price is only one of four numbers that decide what a buyer really pays.

lines.text: Kelley Blue Book says the average new vehicle went for $50,089 in August 2026, the first month of 2026 above $50,000.
lines.say: Kelley Blue Book says the average new vehicle went for fifty thousand eighty-nine dollars in August twenty twenty-six, the first month of twenty twenty-six above fifty thousand.

lines.text: The average sticker was $51,852. So buyers paid about $1,763 under sticker, on average.
lines.say: The average sticker was fifty-one thousand eight hundred fifty-two dollars. So buyers paid about seventeen hundred sixty-three dollars under sticker, on average.

lines.text: Here's the surprise. In one example coming up, a two-point bump in the loan rate costs about $2,000.
lines.say: Here's the surprise. In one example coming up, a two-point bump in the loan rate costs about two thousand dollars.

lines.text: That's more than the whole $1,763 average discount, and it never shows up on the window sticker.
lines.say: That's more than the whole seventeen hundred sixty-three dollar average discount, and it never shows up on the window sticker.

lines.text: So here's the whole purchase in order, with the real rules and the math at every step.
lines.say: So here's the whole purchase in order, with the real rules and the math at every step.

lines.text: Chapter one. The budget, built on total cost.
lines.say: Chapter one. The budget, built on total cost.

lines.text: Most buyers walk in thinking about one number: the monthly payment.
lines.say: Most buyers walk in thinking about one number: the monthly payment.

lines.text: In the second quarter of 2026, the average new-car payment was $765 a month, according to Experian.
lines.say: In the second quarter of twenty twenty-six, the average new-car payment was seven hundred sixty-five dollars a month, according to Experian.

lines.text: The trouble is, a payment can be made to fit almost any budget, just by stretching the loan.
lines.say: The trouble is, a payment can be made to fit almost any budget, just by stretching the loan.

lines.text: Stretching lowers the payment but adds interest. We ran that math in our October eleventh video.
lines.say: Stretching lowers the payment but adds interest. We ran that math in our October eleventh video.

lines.text: Careful buyers flip it around: the total first, then the payment.
lines.say: Careful buyers flip it around: the total first, then the payment.

lines.text: That total is called the out-the-door price: the car, the fees, the add-ons and the taxes, all in one number.
lines.say: That total is called the out-the-door price: the car, the fees, the add-ons and the taxes, all in one number.

lines.text: Here's an example. Say the agreed price is $38,000.
lines.say: Here's an example. Say the agreed price is thirty-eight thousand dollars.

lines.text: Add $1,500 in dealer add-ons, which is an example amount.
lines.say: Add fifteen hundred dollars in dealer add-ons, which is an example amount.

lines.text: Then a $500 documentation fee, also an example.
lines.say: Then a five hundred dollar documentation fee, also an example.

lines.text: And 6% sales tax on the $38,000 price, which comes to $2,280.
lines.say: And six percent sales tax on the thirty-eight thousand dollar price, which comes to two thousand two hundred eighty dollars.

lines.text: Plus $400 for title and registration in this example, and the real total is $42,680.
lines.say: Plus four hundred dollars for title and registration in this example, and the real total is forty-two thousand six hundred eighty dollars.

lines.text: That's $4,680 more than the handshake price, and that's the number the budget has to cover.
lines.say: That's four thousand six hundred eighty dollars more than the handshake price, and that's the number the budget has to cover.

lines.text: Chapter two. Why the financing comes first.
lines.say: Chapter two. Why the financing comes first.

lines.text: When a dealer arranges a buyer's loan, the lender quotes the dealer a rate. The CFPB calls that the buy rate.
lines.say: When a dealer arranges a buyer's loan, the lender quotes the dealer a rate. The C F P B calls that the buy rate.

lines.text: The rate offered to the buyer can be higher, and the difference helps pay the dealer. Say a 6.35% buy rate is offered at 8.35%.
lines.say: The rate offered to the buyer can be higher, and the difference helps pay the dealer. Say a six point three five percent buy rate is offered at eight point three five.

lines.text: That's just an example. Lenders often cap the markup, and the CFPB notes the rate is negotiable.
lines.say: That's just an example. Lenders often cap the markup, and the C F P B notes the rate is negotiable.

lines.text: Now the math. Take a $35,000 loan over 60 months at 6.35%. The payment is about $682.
lines.say: Now the math. Take a thirty-five thousand dollar loan over sixty months at six point three five percent. The payment is about six hundred eighty-two dollars.

lines.text: At 8.35%, it's about $716. Only about $33 more a month, which is easy to wave through.
lines.say: At eight point three five percent, it's about seven hundred sixteen. Only about thirty-three dollars more a month, which is easy to wave through.

lines.text: But over five years, total interest goes from about $5,942 to $7,933.
lines.say: But over five years, total interest goes from about fifty-nine hundred forty-two dollars to seventy-nine hundred thirty-three.

lines.text: That's $1,991.53 more: the two thousand dollars from the start.
lines.say: That's nineteen hundred ninety-one dollars and fifty-three cents more: the two thousand dollars from the start.

lines.text: So some buyers line up a loan offer from a bank or credit union before they ever visit the lot.
lines.say: So some buyers line up a loan offer from a bank or credit union before they ever visit the lot.

lines.text: Then the dealer's offer has something to beat, and the buyer can take whichever rate is lower.
lines.say: Then the dealer's offer has something to beat, and the buyer can take whichever rate is lower.

lines.text: Worried about credit checks? The CFPB says auto-loan inquiries within a 14 to 45 day window generally count as one.
lines.say: Worried about credit checks? The C F P B says auto-loan inquiries within a fourteen to forty-five day window generally count as one.

lines.text: Credit scores matter too. In the second quarter of 2026, Experian's average new-car rate ran from 4.41% to 13.52%.
lines.say: Credit scores matter too. In the second quarter of twenty twenty-six, Experian's average new-car rate ran from four point four one percent to thirteen point five two percent.

lines.text: Chapter three. The price, out the door.
lines.say: Chapter three. The price, out the door.

lines.text: First, the backdrop. Here's the average price paid for a new vehicle in most months of 2026, from Kelley Blue Book.
lines.say: First, the backdrop. Here's the average price paid for a new vehicle in most months of twenty twenty-six, from Kelley Blue Book.

lines.text: It started January at $49,191 and crossed $50,000 in August.
lines.say: It started January at forty-nine thousand one hundred ninety-one dollars and crossed fifty thousand in August.

lines.text: Cox Automotive says the average used-car listing was $27,239 in August 2026, up 7% from a year earlier.
lines.say: Cox Automotive says the average used-car listing was twenty-seven thousand two hundred thirty-nine dollars in August twenty twenty-six, up seven percent from a year earlier.

lines.text: Automakers do offer deals. In August 2026, incentives averaged 6.5% of the transaction price, down from 7.2% a year before.
lines.say: Automakers do offer deals. In August twenty twenty-six, incentives averaged six point five percent of the transaction price, down from seven point two percent a year before.

lines.text: So how do buyers find a fair price? Many start with what similar cars actually sell for, not the sticker.
lines.say: So how do buyers find a fair price? Many start with what similar cars actually sell for, not the sticker.

lines.text: In August 2026, that average gap was about 3.4% below sticker.
lines.say: In August twenty twenty-six, that average gap was about three point four percent below sticker.

lines.text: Then they ask several dealers for written out-the-door quotes, often by email, to compare side by side.
lines.say: Then they ask several dealers for written out-the-door quotes, often by email, to compare side by side.

lines.text: Why out-the-door? Because a low price with big fees can cost more than a higher price with none.
lines.say: Why out-the-door? Because a low price with big fees can cost more than a higher price with none.

lines.text: And they keep the price talk separate from the loan and the trade-in, so one number can't quietly pay for another.
lines.say: And they keep the price talk separate from the loan and the trade-in, so one number can't quietly pay for another.

lines.text: Chapter four. The fees and the add-ons.
lines.say: Chapter four. The fees and the add-ons.

lines.text: First, the documentation fee: what dealers charge for paperwork. The rules depend on the state.
lines.say: First, the documentation fee: what dealers charge for paperwork. The rules depend on the state.

lines.text: California caps it at $85 for most dealers. A 2025 bill to raise the cap to as much as $260 was vetoed.
lines.say: California caps it at eighty-five dollars for most dealers. A twenty twenty-five bill to raise the cap to as much as two hundred sixty dollars was vetoed.

lines.text: Florida has no cap, and CarEdge's 2026 survey puts the average Florida fee near $1,000. Same paperwork, very different bill.
lines.say: Florida has no cap, and CarEdge's twenty twenty-six survey puts the average Florida fee near a thousand dollars. Same paperwork, very different bill.

lines.text: Next, add-ons: things like paint protection, nitrogen in the tires, or window etching that show up on the contract.
lines.say: Next, add-ons: things like paint protection, nitrogen in the tires, or window etching that show up on the contract.

lines.text: The FTC's CARS Rule, meant to curb surprise add-ons, was struck down by a federal appeals court in January 2025.
lines.say: The F T C's CARS Rule, meant to curb surprise add-ons, was struck down by a federal appeals court in January twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: The FTC formally pulled it from the rulebook in February 2026. So add-on rules now come mostly from the states.
lines.say: The F T C formally pulled it from the rulebook in February twenty twenty-six. So add-on rules now come mostly from the states.

lines.text: California's own version, the CARS Act, took effect on October 1, 2026.
lines.say: California's own version, the CARS Act, took effect on October first, twenty twenty-six.

scene.headline: California's CARS Act takes effect October 1

lines.text: It requires a total price in ads and add-ons labeled optional, and it bans add-ons with no benefit, like an oil change on an electric car.
lines.say: It requires a total price in ads and add-ons labeled optional, and it bans add-ons with no benefit, like an oil change on an electric car.

lines.text: Now the math on financed add-ons. Say $1,500 of them get rolled into the loan at 6.35% for 72 months.
lines.say: Now the math on financed add-ons. Say fifteen hundred dollars of them get rolled into the loan at six point three five percent for seventy-two months.

lines.text: The buyer pays $1,807.77 for them, including $307.77 in interest.
lines.say: The buyer pays eighteen hundred seven dollars and seventy-seven cents for them, including three hundred seven dollars and seventy-seven cents in interest.

lines.text: Chapter five. The trade-in, and signing day.
lines.say: Chapter five. The trade-in, and signing day.

lines.text: Trading in the old car can save money in a way people forget: sales tax.
lines.say: Trading in the old car can save money in a way people forget: sales tax.

lines.text: Most states tax only the difference between the new price and the trade-in. California is one exception that taxes the full price.
lines.say: Most states tax only the difference between the new price and the trade-in. California is one exception that taxes the full price.

lines.text: For example, a $38,000 car and a $15,000 trade, with 6% tax. Without the credit, tax is $2,280.
lines.say: For example, a thirty-eight thousand dollar car and a fifteen thousand dollar trade, with six percent tax. Without the credit, tax is two thousand two hundred eighty dollars.

lines.text: With it, the tax is on $23,000, which is $1,380. That's $900 kept in the buyer's pocket.
lines.say: With it, the tax is on twenty-three thousand dollars, which is one thousand three hundred eighty dollars. That's nine hundred dollars kept in the buyer's pocket.

lines.text: Edmunds says 29.6% of trade-ins toward new cars had negative equity in the second quarter of 2026.
lines.say: Edmunds says twenty-nine point six percent of trade-ins toward new cars had negative equity in the second quarter of twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: Negative equity means the owner owes more on the old car than it's worth. The average gap was $6,884.
lines.say: Negative equity means the owner owes more on the old car than it's worth. The average gap was six thousand eight hundred eighty-four dollars.

lines.text: That gap usually gets rolled into the new loan. Here's that slice alone, at 6.35% for 72 months.
lines.say: That gap usually gets rolled into the new loan. Here's that slice alone, at six point three five percent for seventy-two months.

lines.text: It adds $115.23 to every payment and about $1,412 in interest, for a car the buyer no longer owns.
lines.say: It adds a hundred fifteen dollars and twenty-three cents to every payment and about fourteen hundred twelve dollars in interest, for a car the buyer no longer owns.

lines.text: In Edmunds' data, those buyers paid $944 a month on average in Q2 2026, versus $777 for all new-car loans.
lines.say: In Edmunds' data, those buyers paid nine hundred forty-four dollars a month on average in the second quarter of twenty twenty-six, versus seven hundred seventy-seven for all new-car loans.

lines.text: And their projected interest averaged $16,270, compared with $9,811 for the average new-car buyer.
lines.say: And their projected interest averaged sixteen thousand two hundred seventy dollars, compared with nine thousand eight hundred eleven dollars for the average new-car buyer.

lines.text: Some owners in that spot keep the old car longer and pay it down first, so the gap shrinks before they trade.
lines.say: Some owners in that spot keep the old car longer and pay it down first, so the gap shrinks before they trade.

lines.text: And now, the rules on signing day.
lines.say: And now, the rules on signing day.

lines.text: Here's a myth: that every car purchase comes with three days to change your mind.
lines.say: Here's a myth: that every car purchase comes with three days to change your mind.

lines.text: The FTC says federal law doesn't require dealers to give buyers three days to cancel. Its Cooling-Off Rule doesn't cover cars.
lines.say: The F T C says federal law doesn't require dealers to give buyers three days to cancel. Its Cooling-Off Rule doesn't cover cars.

lines.text: California now does. Under its CARS Act, used cars priced at $50,000 or less can be returned within three days.
lines.say: California now does. Under its CARS Act, used cars priced at fifty thousand dollars or less can be returned within three days.

lines.text: That ends if the car's been driven more than 400 miles,
lines.say: That ends if the car's been driven more than four hundred miles,

lines.text: and the dealer can charge a restocking fee, though the law caps it.
lines.say: and the dealer can charge a restocking fee, though the law caps it.

lines.text: On used cars, the FTC requires a Buyers Guide in the window, saying whether there's a warranty or the car's sold as is.
lines.say: On used cars, the F T C requires a Buyers Guide in the window, saying whether there's a warranty or the car's sold as is.

lines.text: As is means the dealer won't pay for problems after the sale. That's why some used-car buyers pay for an independent inspection first.
lines.say: As is means the dealer won't pay for problems after the sale. That's why some used-car buyers pay for an independent inspection first.

lines.text: One newer rule can help new-car buyers: a federal tax deduction for car loan interest, for tax years 2025 through 2028.
lines.say: One newer rule can help new-car buyers: a federal tax deduction for car loan interest, for tax years twenty twenty-five through twenty twenty-eight.

lines.text: The IRS finalized the details in September 2026. The car has to be new, assembled in the US, for personal use, with the loan taken out after 2024.
lines.say: The IRS finalized the details in September twenty twenty-six. The car has to be new, assembled in the US, for personal use, with the loan taken out after twenty twenty-four.

lines.text: Leases don't count. It phases out between $100K and $150K of modified adjusted gross income, or $200K to $250K for joint filers.
lines.say: Leases don't count. It phases out between a hundred and a hundred fifty thousand dollars of modified adjusted gross income, or two hundred to two hundred fifty thousand for joint filers.

lines.text: And interest on rolled-in negative equity isn't deductible. Only the part of the loan that bought the new car counts.
lines.say: And interest on rolled-in negative equity isn't deductible. Only the part of the loan that bought the new car counts.

lines.text: What's it worth? On our $35,000 example at 6.35%, first-year interest is $2,045.77.
lines.say: What's it worth? On our thirty-five thousand dollar example at six point three five percent, first-year interest is two thousand forty-five dollars and seventy-seven cents.

lines.text: It's a deduction, not a credit. In the 22% bracket, that's worth about $450 in tax; in the 12% bracket, about $245.

lines.text: Helpful, but a first-year value of about $450 is smaller than the roughly $1,992 a two-point markup cost over five years in our example.

post.yt_desc:
The average new vehicle sold for $50,089 in August 2026, but the sticker is only one of four numbers that decide what a buyer pays. This guide walks through buying a car in order: budgeting on the out-the-door price, how dealer-arranged loan rates work and what a 2-point markup costs, finding a fair price, doc fees and add-ons (including California's CARS Act, in effect October 1, 2026), trade-ins and negative equity, and the signing-day rules, including the new federal car loan interest deduction. All loan examples are labeled hypotheticals with fixed rates and no fees. It ends with the common mistakes and a one-screen checklist.
